title: Rational geometric components through mixed nodal and regular point blowups
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$, residue field $k$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X_0\to T$ be integral and H-projective [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-kun-projective]. Let $X_m\xrightarrow{b_m}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0$ be a finite tower in which every $X_i$ is integral and Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact) [pqf-def-locnoeth], and $b_{i+1}$ is the blowup of one reduced closed point $z_i$ of the special fibre $(X_i)_k$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-closed-immersion]. At every centre assume one of the following two conditions: (a) $X_i\to T$ is flat and finitely presented, with smooth generic fibre and reduced pure one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres over some open neighbourhood of $z_i$ in $X_i$, and $X_i$ is not regular at $z_i$; or (b) $\mathcal O_{X_i,z_i}$ is a regular local ring of dimension two [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. In (a), nodal means that every nonsmooth closed geometric fibre point over an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. For $j\leq m$, write $g_j:X_j\to X_0$ for the composite. For every algebraically closed $\Omega$ and geometric point $c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_0$, the reduction $B_{j,c}=(X_j\times_{X_0}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\mathrm{red}}$ is of dimension at most one, has finitely many irreducible components, and each positive-dimensional irreducible component is isomorphic over $\Omega$ to $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction, def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-p1-standard]. For each such component $L\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ at stage $j$, its scheme-theoretic strict transform under $b_{j+1}$, computed from the morphism $L\to X_j$, is isomorphic to $L$ over $\Omega$ and is a closed subscheme of $B_{j+1,c}$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. No perfectness of $k$ or separability of centre residue fields is assumed, and $m=0$ is permitted.

source.place: Tag 080E (lemma-strict-transform), together with resolve.tex Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup) and Tag 0AGR (lemma-blowup-regular); nodal exceptional fibres from the xy=pi^n calculation of de Jong Lemma 3.13 proof, printed p.609. Agent-formulated induction on geometric components, carrying returned Steps 3 and 8; archival de Jong PDF WANTED, primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Fix $c:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X_0$ and put $Y_j=X_j\times_{X_0}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $B_j=(Y_j)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Each reduced point centre has a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, since its ambient scheme is Noetherian. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] each arrow is proper, hence finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], $Y_j$ is finite type over $\Omega$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes it Noetherian. Its underlying space, also that of $B_j$, has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. At $j=0$, $Y_0=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, giving the induction base including the entire assertion for $m=0$.

source.place: Blowing up, properness; agent induction setup (finite-type ideals on Noetherian schemes).

proof.text: For a centre $z=z_j$, its residue field $l=\kappa(z)$ is finite over $k$: $z$ is closed in the special fibre, which is finite type over $k$ (initially $X_0$ is H-projective and subsequent blowups are finite type); apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] on an affine neighbourhood in that fibre. If the image of $c$ in $T$ is not the closed point, $Z=z\times_{X_0}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is empty. Otherwise $Z$ is a closed subscheme of $z\times_k\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$: the additional equations express equality of the two maps to the separated $k$-scheme $(X_0)_k$. Indeed [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes $X_0\to T$ proper, so [def-weil-proper-morphism] makes its base change to $k$ separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] the larger product has algebra $l\otimes_k\Omega$, spanned over $\Omega$ by a $k$-basis of $l$. Thus $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ finite dimensional over $\Omega$, possibly zero. It is Artinian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] and has finitely many points by [lem-sfb-artinian-spectrum-finite]. For every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $D$, the finite-dimensional domain $D/\mathfrak p$ is a field (multiplication by a nonzero element is injective, hence surjective), and equals $\Omega$: the minimal polynomial of any element splits into linear factors. Thus every reduced point of $Z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. This permits nonreduced $D$ and inseparable $l/k$.

source.place: Tags 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), 00J6 (lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra); finite centre after geometric base change.

proof.text: In case (a), shrink to an affine open neighbourhood of $z$ contained in the stipulated nodal neighbourhood. The restricted family is flat finitely presented with smooth generic fibre and the stated nodal geometric fibres; the affine restriction is finitely presented: its coordinate algebra is finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$, hence finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Apply [lem-sfb-nodal-trait-finite-singular-charts] to this restriction. Since $z$ is nonregular, it has the common pointed etale chart with $M_n=\operatorname{Spec}R'[x,y]/(xy-\pi^n)$, $n\ge2$. The exceptional geometric fibre of its point blowup is one $\mathbf P^1$ for $n=2$, and two $\mathbf P^1$'s meeting in a point for $n>2$, by [lem-sfb-dvr-nodal-chart-blowup-calculus]. To use this over the specified $\Omega$-point of $Z$, extend its residue-field map to the chart point using [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed]; the chart residue extension is finite separable. By [lem-sfb-flat-pullback-blowup-chart-restrictions], shrink the etale neighbourhood to isolate that point; both pulled-back centre ideals are then the reduced point ideals. Their blowups give the same geometric fibre over this chosen lift. Hence the exceptional fibre of $b_{j+1}$ over each reduced point of $Z$ has exactly the asserted one-line or two-line description over $\Omega$. This uses only nodality near this centre.

source.place: Tags 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), 0CDC (example-blowup); point isolation and flat base change in proof of Tag 0CDE.

proof.text: In case (b), put $R=\mathcal O_{X_j,z}$, a regular local ring of dimension two. Its canonical local-spectrum morphism is flat and pulls the reduced centre back to the maximal ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]. The comparison of [lem-sfb-flat-pullback-blowup-chart-restrictions] therefore identifies its exceptional fibre with that of $b_{j+1}$ over $z$. By [lem-sfb-local-surface-maximal-blowup-geometry], this fibre is $\mathbf P^1_l$. For each reduced point of $Z$, base change along its map $l\to\Omega$ gives $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$; the base-change identification is just associativity in [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Consequently the reduced inverse image of $Z$ is a finite union of closed projective lines in either case (a) or (b): every point maps to one of its finitely many reduced points, and the corresponding geometric fibres cover the underlying inverse image. Nilpotents in $Z$ do not add points.

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), assertion (1), and geometric base change of the exceptional projective line.

proof.text: Assume the dimension and component assertions at stage $j$, and let $L\cong\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ be one of its positive-dimensional components, given its reduced closed subscheme structure in $Y_j$. Let $\mathcal I$ be the centre ideal on $X_j$ and $J=\mathcal I\mathcal O_L$. Its vanishing set is contained in $Z$; hence it is finite and does not contain the generic point of $L$. On each of the two affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t]$ of [def-sc-p1-standard], $J$ is an ideal of $\Omega[t]$. It is nonzero because it is the unit ideal at the generic point. By [lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid] it equals $(f)$ for a nonzero polynomial $f$. Multiplication by $f$ identifies the chart's structure sheaf with this ideal (the polynomial ring is a domain). Thus $J$ is invertible, including when the centre intersection is empty or nonreduced. By [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] the strict transform of the morphism $L\to X_j$ is $\operatorname{Bl}_J L$; by [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso] its projection to $L$ is an isomorphism. No separability is used in this argument.

source.place: Tag 080E (lemma-strict-transform), assertion (1); algebra.tex Tag 030A (lemma-polynomial-domain-normal), PID field case.

proof.text: Write $L^{\mathrm{st}}$ for that strict transform. By [def-nagata-strict-transform] it is a closed subscheme of $L\times_{X_j}X_{j+1}$. The closed immersion $L\hookrightarrow Y_j$, pulled back by $X_{j+1}\to X_j$, gives a closed immersion $L\times_{X_j}X_{j+1}\hookrightarrow Y_{j+1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Hence $L^{\mathrm{st}}$ is closed in $Y_{j+1}$. As it is isomorphic to the reduced scheme $L$, its map factors through $B_{j+1}$: affine-locally the defining surjection kills every nilpotent, since the target ring is reduced. The resulting map from the reduction ring remains surjective, so this factorization is a closed immersion. By the closure definition, its support is the closure of the inverse image of $L\setminus Z$; this is dense in $L$ since $Z$ is finite. This proves exactly the claimed scheme-theoretic strict-transform assertion, including its specified $\Omega$-structure.

source.place: Definition strict transform immediately preceding Tag 080E; schemes.tex Definition 01J4, reduction by the nilradical.

proof.text: By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement], $Y_{j+1}\to Y_j$ is an isomorphism away from $Z$. Each point outside the inverse image of $Z$ therefore lies either on the inverse image of one of the finitely many old lines, or over a zero-dimensional old component. The former points lie in the corresponding $L^{\mathrm{st}}$ by its closure definition. Each zero-dimensional component of the finite-type $\Omega$-scheme $B_j$ is a single closed reduced $\Omega$-point, by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]; if it is outside $Z$, its inverse image is again a closed point. Points over $Z$ lie on the finitely many exceptional lines in Steps 3--4. Thus the support of $B_{j+1}$ is covered by finitely many closed subschemes isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ and finitely many closed points. An irreducible subset of a finite union of closed sets lies in one of them: otherwise its intersections with them would express it as a finite union of proper closed subsets. Consequently every irreducible component is one of these lines or one of these points. A proper irreducible closed subset of a projective line is a point, as its intersection with either standard affine chart is cut out by a nonzero polynomial, with finitely many roots. Hence the dimension is at most one, and every positive-dimensional component is a whole projective line. This completes the induction for every $j$ and every $c$.

source.place: Blowup complement and Tag 080E; agent finite-union induction on reduced geometric components.
